conclusion: A generic organic interface on a non-belt build plate must not be removed merely because lower-road or unsupported-span checks cannot find a foundation beneath it. When regular filling produces no interface in that bed region, the existing legal contact contour is a bounded fallback; do not emit narrow medial-axis fragments instead. Independently, first-layer brim width normalization must be transactional: if projection, routing or coverage validation fails, restore the original support collection instead of exporting partial width-normalized or spliced paths. This preserves the brim and configured process parameters. Continuity of the interface is not a requirement, and failed normalization is not proof that overlapping geometry is safe.

No other model was used for acceptance, and upper-layer bearing was not part of this task.
